name: Alert
description: Displays a brief, important message that attracts the user's attention without interrupting the user's task. Dynamically rendered alerts are automatically announced by screen readers.

roles.description: Implicitly aria-live='assertive' + aria-atomic='true'. Interrupts the screen reader immediately — reserve it for genuinely urgent messages.
Implicitly aria-live='polite' + aria-atomic='true'. Waits for a pause. This is the right default for most messages.
Implicitly aria-live='polite'. For sequential additions where order matters — chat, activity feeds.

required_attributes.description: Prefer the role over raw aria-live: it carries the right live/atomic defaults and also gives the region a landmark-ish identity.

optional_attributes.description: Only needed when no role fits. role='status' already implies polite; role='alert' already implies assertive. Never use assertive for anything non-urgent.
true = re-announce the whole region on any change; false = announce only what changed. Implicitly true for alert/status.
Which mutations trigger an announcement. Default 'additions text' is almost always right — changing it is a common way to break announcements.

notes: Alert is not interactive — no keyboard interaction needed

THE critical rule: the live region container must ALREADY be in the DOM, empty, before you put text in it. Injecting a
message
in one go frequently announces nothing — the screen reader never saw the region appear.
Use role='status' (polite) by default. role='alert' (assertive) interrupts whatever the user is currently hearing — reserve it for genuine urgency, like a session about to expire or a failed payment.
Never put role='alert' on a container that is always present and populated at page load — it announces on every page load, for nothing.
Announce only text. Interactive content in a live region cannot be reached: an 'Undo' button inside role='alert' is announced but nobody can Tab to it in time before the toast disappears.
For less urgent info use role=status with aria-live=polite
Toasts that auto-dismiss are a time limit (RAWeb 13.1). Either do not auto-dismiss, or make the timeout adjustable, and never put the only copy of important information in one.
Do not put role='alert' on an error summary you also want to move focus to — use focus OR the live region, not both, or it is announced twice.
Empty a live region before writing a new identical message, or the screen reader may not detect a change and stay silent.
native_element: none — output is close for calculated results, but role=alert / role=status is the mechanism

raweb_criteria.reason: THE criterion for this pattern. Status messages must be rendered to assistive technologies without moving focus — that is exactly what a live region is.
The alert's role must be exposed so the message is announced at all.
An error styled only in red is invisible to a user who cannot distinguish it. Pair colour with an icon and text.
An alert that auto-dismisses on a timer is a time limit on reading it — the user must be able to control it, or it must not disappear.
